personality: 1 iOS-Native Clean (Adapted for One UI 6 with bento grids, large reachable headers, and soft pastel accents)
personality_one_liner: A clean, highly readable productivity canvas featuring large reachable headers, frosted glass, and rounded bento-style note cards.

spacing.rule: Generous spacing. Utilize large top margins (3xl) to replicate One UI's reachable header design.

do's: Use on the top sticky header when content scrolls behind it
Use on the bottom floating formatting toolbar in the note editor
Use on modal scrims and floating context menus
dont's: Do not use on individual note cards in lists
Do not use on the main surface background

screens.name: Home / All Notes
screens.purpose: Main bento grid/list of all user notes with search, sort filters, and a floating FAB for creation.

states.loading: Centered spinner with a subtle brand tint.
states.empty: Illustration of a blank notebook page, message 'No notes yet', and 'Create Note' CTA.
states.error: Message 'Unable to load notes' with a retry button.

screens.layout: Large scrollable area with a 'reachable' top header (large title 'Notes'). Below the header, a toggle for Grid/List view and a Filter icon. Notes are displayed as rounded bento cards (`surfaceSecondary`) with title, preview text, date, and an optional left border stripe indicating folder color. A Floating Action Button (FAB) sits at the bottom right. A sticky frosted glass header appears when scrolled.

screens.name: Note Editor
screens.purpose: Full-screen rich text editor and drawing canvas with immersive top and bottom toolbars.
screens.layout: Top sticky toolbar (transparent or frosted if scrolled) with Back, PDF import, Undo/Redo, and More menu. Large title input field, followed by body text input extending flex: 1. Bottom formatting toolbar (keyboard-avoiding) containing bold, italic, list, checklist, and drawing toggle. When drawing mode is active, the bottom toolbar switches to pen, highlighter, eraser, and color picker tools.

screens.name: Drawer / Folders
screens.purpose: Slide-out navigation for organizing notes by folders, tags, and accessing settings.
screens.layout: Standard drawer layout. Top section shows user profile or app logo. List items for 'All Notes', 'Shared Notes', 'Trash', and user-created folders. Folders have a small colored dot indicator (`brandTertiary`, `warning`, `info`, etc.). Bottom link to Settings.

screens.name: Note Lock Modal
screens.purpose: Passcode or biometric prompt to unlock secured notes.

states.error: Shake animation on text input with 'Incorrect passcode' red text.

screens.layout: Full screen overlay with a frosted glass backdrop. Minimal 3D lock illustration centered. Large typography prompt 'Enter passcode'. Pin pad or numeric input below. 'Cancel' button below the pad.

empty_notes.alt: Minimal blank notebook on wooden desk

drawer_header_bg.alt: Minimal notebook folder leaning on surface

instructions_to_main_agent: Adhere strictly to the monochromatic/botanical palette (`#7B8C73` Sage Green). Do NOT use orange, blue, indigo, purple, or terracotta anywhere in the app, as these are strictly banned by the system rules.

Replicate the One UI 6 aesthetic: use generous spacing (large `3xl` top margin for the 'Notes' header so it's thumb-reachable), highly rounded corners on note cards (`lg` or `xl`), and clean, legible typography.

For the Home screen bento cards, use `surfaceSecondary` with `lg` padding. If a note belongs to a folder, show a small left-border vertical stripe or a colored dot using subtle pastel tokens or the folder's assigned color.
Implement frosted glass (`expo-blur`) heavily on the sticky top header when scrolling the list, and on the floating bottom formatting toolbar in the note editor.
Ensure the Note Editor uses `KeyboardAvoidingView` perfectly so the bottom toolbar rests directly on top of the virtual keyboard.
Do NOT use drop shadows on individual bento cards; rely on `surfaceSecondary` color contrast against the pure white/black `surface` canvas. Only use shadows for the FAB and bottom sheets.
Use standard Ionicons but prefer rounded/outline variants. Keep weights consistent across all icons.
